title: What Stonehenge was for
summary: Many aspects of Stonehenge, including how it was built and what it was used for, remain subject to debate. Its builders left no written records.
why: It is Europe's most famous prehistoric monument, built over fifteen centuries.
question: What was Stonehenge for, and how were its stones moved?
evidence: Begun about 3100 BCE; sarsen circle 2600–2400 BCE; bluestones placed 2400–2200 BCE; aligned on solstices; cremation cemetery in an early phase.
wouldSettle: Excavated evidence of transport routes and of activities at the site, dated phase by phase.

theories.name: Monument to the dead
theories.idea: A burial and cremation site; nearby Durrington Walls represented the living.

theories.name: Solar calendar or observatory
theories.idea: Its solstice alignments suggest a celestial observatory function.

theories.name: Healing centre
theories.idea: Wainwright and Darvill proposed a prehistoric healing site, like Lourdes.

theories.name: Symbol of unification
theories.idea: It marked peace and unity as Neolithic Britain culturally unified.
